items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Chick Webb was playing and Basie's band was playing... I had the thing going... Chick had Ella, we had Billie.

ctx.x: brought that band to New York and Walter Page - was Basie in that band that came here?

Walter Page did not join it till 1932. When Bennie came to New York City he upset New York City with "Driving Me Crazy," which was Moten's Swing they played, then. And that's the time when they had the 5-band tour with Blanche Calloway, Johnson (Happy Pals) (Hakapais?), Chick Webb. Everybody would get in the buses and make the tour down through . . . . . . You know how things were. You have somebody go around and say, "There's going to be a battle of bands," and the musicians just splitting up the money. You…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I knew the Chick Webbs and Sid Catletts and what have you, but to know these peoples and to have that background, you see.

ctx.x: She joined us - we came into New York in '36, when Billie Holiday joined us in 1937. She stayed with us nearly a year. Things were going and we finally got so that we could leave the Palace Theatre to go to the Apollo Loews State. Naturally when you leave the Loews State you can go from the Loews State to the other theatre and then finally when you was the epitome was when you could play the Paramount, because it was an outmoded thing that

you were going to play the Palace, because the Palace had always established itself in another vein and they did not go with the status quo so far as the Benny Goodmans and the Chick Webbs and the Jimmy Luncefords and what have you. They didn't go along with the jazz.
Was Miss Billie Holiday the first vocalist you had with the band?
